options: When a ship is at its extreme pitch angle.
When a ship is at its extreme pitch and roll angles, simultaneously.
CD0111 — Heavy Weather Damage - Containe.answer: When a ship is at its extreme pitch angle.

CD0111 — Heavy Weather Damage - Containe.question: Which of these motions has a marked effect on a ship’s stability, whilst also affecting container corner posts and the cargo securing system in general?
CD0111 — Heavy Weather Damage - Containe.answer: Heaving

CD0111 — Heavy Weather Damage - Containe.question: When does a container experience a force of 100% of its weight plus cargo?
CD0111 — Heavy Weather Damage - Containe.answer: When heaving, in linear motion.

CD0111 — Heavy Weather Damage - Containe.question: For a container stowed in a position equidistant from the roll and pitch axes of your ship, what would reduce the accelerations to one quarter?
CD0111 — Heavy Weather Damage - Containe.answer: Doubling the roll period.

CD0111 — Heavy Weather Damage - Containe.question: With respect to twistlock springs, what would ensure their safe operation?
options: The spring, holding the twistlock cone in the ‘closed’ position, should be resilient.
The spring, holding twistlock cone in a ‘closed’ position, is resilient but loose.
There would be no problem in using left and right-hand twistlocks together.
CD0111 — Heavy Weather Damage - Containe.answer: The spring, holding the twistlock cone in the ‘closed’ position, should be resilient.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Which statement is correct:
options: The operator is not to be contacted by the vessel after regular office hours.
The operator is there to assist you, and can be contacted normally during office hours only.
The operator is there to assist you, and can be contacted at all times when necessary.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: The operator is there to assist you, and can be contacted at all times when necessary.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: How often and when must temperature reports be sent to the office?
options: On Monday, Wednesday and Friday, immediately after departure from the load port.
On a daily basis, starting at departure from the first load port.
On a daily basis, starting after closing the first cooling section in the first load port.
On a daily basis, but only if temperature problems are encountered.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: On a daily basis, starting after closing the first cooling section in the first load port.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: A carrying instruction should always contain:
options: Delivery air temperature, return air temperature, seawater salinity and humidity.
Delivery air temperature, maximum CO2 level, dew point, humidity and speed of circulation fans.
Delivery air temperature, maximum CO2 level, speed of circulation fans and shock treatment instructions if so required.
Return air temperature, set point, humidity, and shock treatment instructions if so required.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Delivery air temperature, maximum CO2 level, speed of circulation fans and shock treatment instructions if so required.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: When different temperatures are required in different compartments it is important to write down the different temperatures per compartment in the stowage plan:
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Yes

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Which statement is correct:
options: The vessel always has to comply with the speed instructions and does not have to comply with the Zero Damage instructions.
The vessel always has to comply with the speed instructions to make sure to arrive on time at the discharge port, no matter what.
The vessel has to comply with the speed instructions, but there should be no compromise to the Zero Damage condition of the cargo.
The vessel has to comply with the speed instructions and never stop or change course or change speed.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: The vessel has to comply with the speed instructions, but there should be no compromise to the Zero Damage condition of the cargo.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Take this example through the 4th step of the 4-step load questions. Will the cargo negatively affect the condition of other cargo?
options: Yes, the cargo will negatively affect the condition of other cargo.
No, the cargo will not negatively affect the condition of other cargo.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: No, the cargo will not negatively affect the condition of other cargo.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Rejected cargo has to be set-aside in a protected cargo shed area on the quay.
Rejected cargo has to go straight back to the terminal.
Rejected cargo has to be loaded anyway into the cargo hold.
Rejected cargo has to go back to the receiver.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Rejected cargo has to be set-aside in a protected cargo shed area on the quay.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Take this example through the 3rd step of the 4-step load questions. Will it be possible to load the cargo safely, fast and easily?
options: Yes, it will be possible to load the cargo safely, fast and easily.
No, it will not be possible to load the cargo safely, fast and easily.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: No, it will not be possible to load the cargo safely, fast and easily.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Take this example through the 2nd step of the 4-step load questions. Is it likely that the cargo quality will meet the Receiver’s demand?
options: Yes, the quality of this cargo will meet the Receiver's demand
No, the quality of this cargo is not good and must be rejected.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Yes, the quality of this cargo will meet the Receiver's demand

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Take this example through the 2nd step of the 4-step load questions. Is it likely that the cargo quality will meet the Receiver’s demand?
options: Yes, the cargo quality will meet the Receiver’s demand.
No, the quality of this cargo is not good and must be rejected.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: No, the quality of this cargo is not good and must be rejected.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Take this example through the 1st step of the 4-step load questions. Is the cargo in apparent good order and condition?
options: Yes, the cargo is in apparent good order and condition.
No, the cargo is not in apparent good order and condition.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Yes, the cargo is in apparent good order and condition.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: A pallet has been dropped on the quay, and is badly damaged. Do you sign for this on the Zero Damage Exceptions Checklist?
options: Yes, the pallet is now in damaged condition, so I have to sign for it.
Yes, and I include a remark about time and date.
No, the pallet was in good condition when it left the vessel.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: No, the pallet was in good condition when it left the vessel.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: When the terminal checks the condition of the cargo according to the traffic light system, the red light will be given to:
options: A pallet with a missing carton.
Cargo that is damaged but fit for transportation.
Cargo that is not fit for transportation.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Cargo that is not fit for transportation.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: If the condition of the cargo leads to an amber light according to the traffic light system, the terminal should:
options: Accept the cargo without listing the cargo on the damage sheet.
Mark the cargo with an amber sticker.
Repair and/or replace the cargo or record its damage.
Set the cargo aside and load it only when nobody sees it.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Repair and/or replace the cargo or record its damage.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: What is the definition of Checkpoint Vessel-In?
options: From in the terminal, by handling of the stevedores into the hold.
In the vessel after all handling by the stevedores at the final point of stow in the hold.
From the quay, via the stevedores’ cranes into the hold.
From in the terminal, via the quay, into the hold.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: In the vessel after all handling by the stevedores at the final point of stow in the hold.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: In which case does the T-bar have the highest Maximum Securing Load?
options: With an angle of 30 degrees and 1 lashing applied.
With an angle of 60 degrees and 2 lashings applied.
With an angle of 45 degrees and 2 lashings applied.
With an angle of 30 degrees and 2 lashing applied.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: With an angle of 45 degrees and 2 lashings applied.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Why is it so important to clean and maintain the cargo holds?
options: To avoid the occurrence of stevedore damage in the cargo holds.
To maximise the cargo intake in the cargo holds.
To ensure that food products can be safely loaded in the cargo holds.
To ensure that a nice party can be organised in the cargo holds.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: To ensure that food products can be safely loaded in the cargo holds.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: What is the main purpose of the Vessel Checklist:
options: It’s a guideline on how to handle, stow, load and tally the cargo.
It’s a guideline to prepare the vessel for the different stages in the supply chain.
It’s a tool for the master on how to prepare the vessel before loading.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: It’s a guideline to prepare the vessel for the different stages in the supply chain.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Why is the Checkpoint Vessel-In so important for the vessel?
options: As the terminal will check the cargo quality at this point.
As it is important that the cargo documents are correct.
As the vessel takes responsibility for the cargo at this point.
As this is a part of the Zero Damage policy of the shipping line.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: As the vessel takes responsibility for the cargo at this point.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: What is the most important rule to keep in mind when you use slings?
options: Always minimum 24 pallets must be pre-slung in the hatchsquare.
Always use slings of the same type, SWL and length.
Always use slings to lash the cargo.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Always use slings of the same type, SWL and length.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Which statement is correct?
options: Walking boards must be available just before loading the pre-slung pallets and are compulsory for the crew.
Walking board must be available after opening the hatches and are compulsory for the stevedores.
Walking boards must be left on top of the cargo after completion of loading the hatch square.
Walking boards must be available on arrival in the load port and are compulsory for stevedores and crew.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Walking boards must be available on arrival in the load port and are compulsory for stevedores and crew.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: How do you determine the apparent good order & condition of the cargo?
options: Inspect the pallets like a fruit specialist would do.
Look and inspect the fruit inside the cartons.
Discuss the condition of the cargo with the port captain.
Use common sense, look, smell, and inspect.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Use common sense, look, smell, and inspect.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Why must there always be a deck officer on deck during loading?
options: To monitor, control and enforce the Zero Damage principles.
To monitor and control if damage occurs in the cargo holds.
To monitor, control and enforce the use of the Vessel Checklist.
To monitor and control if it starts to rain.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: To monitor, control and enforce the Zero Damage principles.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: What is a Supply Chain Procedure?
options: A document, which lists the tasks, duties and authorities of the partners who are involved in the supply chain
A document, which describes the local Zero Damage procedure in the port.
A document, which describes the responsibility of the various partners, but it is not a document that you can rely upon.
A document, which has to be issued before the cargo can be transported from its origin to its destination.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: A document, which lists the tasks, duties and authorities of the partners who are involved in the supply chain

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Which picture gives the preferred broken stowage in view of lashing.
options: Drawing A with pallets fore and aft.
Drawing D with pallets fore and port and sb side.
Drawing B with pallets port and sb side.
Drawing C with pallets fore and aft and port and sb side.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Drawing A with pallets fore and aft.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Why do you have to stow the pallets parallel to the centre-line and not parallel to the sides of the cargo hold?
options: Otherwise the discharge of the pallets will be very difficult.
Otherwise you do not get a square for loading the pre-slung pallets.
Otherwise you will not get enough pallets in the cargo hold.
Otherwise you do not get a maximum cargo intake.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Otherwise you do not get a square for loading the pre-slung pallets.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: With an agreed Supply Chain Procedure in place, the responsibility for damages is always clear, because:
options: The Supply Chain Procedure clearly describes which damages have to be recorded.
The Supply Chain Procedure clearly describes where the responsibility for the cargo is handed over from one partner to the next one in the chain.
The Supply Chain Procedure clearly describes that all responsibility for the cargo is with the ship and its crew.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: The Supply Chain Procedure clearly describes where the responsibility for the cargo is handed over from one partner to the next one in the chain.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Why do we have Checkpoints in the supply chain?
options: To check the cargo for damage before it goes out of the terminal.
To check the cargo for damage and establish a handover of responsibility for the cargo from one partner to the next.
To allow the owner of the cargo to examine his goods.
To check that the cargo is going in the right direction in the supply chain.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: To check the cargo for damage and establish a handover of responsibility for the cargo from one partner to the next.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Which statement describes the correct loading sequence?
options: Start with section A and E, then section B and D and finally section C.
Start with section A, then sections B, C and D and finally section E.
Start with section E, then sections B, C and D and finally section A.
Start with section B and D, then section A and E and finally section C.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Start with section A and E, then section B and D and finally section C.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: At the discharge port the custody of the cargo is handed over from the vessel to the terminal. Where should the quality check be done once the pre-slung pallets have been discharged?
options: In the hold before handling the cargo.
On the quay, after lifting the cargo out of the vessel.
In the terminal, where the cargo can be properly scanned.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: In the hold before handling the cargo.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Which rain scenario do you have to use when it rains? It depends on:
options: What kind of vessel you sail on and which discharge port you sail to.
Whether the vessel has the right equipment like tarpaulins, rain covers and so on.
Whether the vessel has spar decks or individual cooling decks.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Whether the vessel has spar decks or individual cooling decks.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Who is responsible for this kind of damage?
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: The stevedores.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: Before opening the hatches, the tweendecks have to be blown clear of debris because:
options: Debris gets stuck in the gratings so cold air is not possible.
Debris is toxic to the consumers.
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: Debris contaminates the cargo.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: What is the main purpose of the rain directives?
options: To protect the cargo in the hatch square when it rains.
To close the hatches immediately when it starts to rain.
To protect the cargo and avoid delays in loading or discharge during light rain.
To discharge the cargo in the right sequence when it rains
CD0112 — Zero Damage.answer: To protect the cargo and avoid delays in loading or discharge during light rain.

CD0112 — Zero Damage.question: What will the terminal check in order to avoid claims before it takes the cargo into custody?
options: The quality and colour of the cargo.
The quality and the quantity of the cargo and its packing.
The quality of the cargo only, the terminal is not responsible for the quantity.
The quantity of the cargo only, the quality is the responsibility of the vessel.

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Who is responsible for issuing an International Ship Security Certificate? Select the ONE correct answer.

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: В чьи обязанности входит выдача международного судового сертификата безопасности? Выберите ОДИН правильный вариант ответа.
CD0115 — Security awareness.answer: Государство флага.

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Uluslararası Gemi Güvenliği Sertifikasını düzenlemeden sorumlu kişi kimdir? BİR doğru cevap seçin.

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: 谁负责颁发国际船只安全证书？ 请选择一个正确答案。

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Quem é responsável pela emissão de um certificado internacional de proteção do navio? Selecione UMA resposta correta.

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: ¿Quién es el responsable de emitir el certificado internacional de protección del buque? Seleccione la ÚNICA respuesta correcta.

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: 누가 국제 선박 보안 인증서 발급을 책임집니까? 올바른 답을 하나 선택하십시오.

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Your ship is entering an area known for pirate activity. Which ONE of the actions listed below is recommended?

To turn off all lights, including navigation lights
To confine all ship’s personnel to one room on-board
To transit at night time only

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Ваше судно входит в район, в котором, как известно, действуют пираты. Какое ОДНО из перечисленных ниже действий рекомендуется предпринять?

Выключить все освещение, включая ходовые огни.

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Geminiz korsan eylemleriyle bilinen bir bölgeye giriyor. Aşağıda listelenen eylemlerin HANGİSİ önerilir?

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: 您的船只将要进入已知存在海盗活动的区域。建议进行以下哪项操作？

将所有船上人员限制在一个船上一个室内
CD0115 — Security awareness.answer: 以最大安全速度穿越

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Seu navio está entrando em uma área conhecida por atividade pirata. Escolha UMA das opções a seguir que indica a ação recomendada?

Confinar toda a tripulação do navio em uma sala a bordo
CD0115 — Security awareness.answer: Transite com velocidade de segurança máxima

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Su buque va a entrar en una zona conocida por su actividad pirata. ¿Cuál es la única acción de las enumeradas a continuación que se recomienda?

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: 여러분의 배가 해적이 활동하는 곳으로 알려진 지역에 진입 중입니다. 아래 행동 중 권장되는 것은 무엇입니까?

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: What is a ‘Declaration of Security’? Select the ONE correct answer.

An agreement (checklist) jointly completed by the Ship Security Officer and the U.S. Coast Guard
A document between the port and the cargo owner, stating the security measures required

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Что представляет собой декларация об охране? Выберите ОДИН правильный вариант ответа.
options: Соглашение (контрольный перечень), достигнутое между судном и портовым средством или другим судном, с указанием мер безопасности, которые должны приниматься каждой из сторон.
Соглашение (контрольный перечень), заполняемое офицером по охране судна и представителем Береговой охраны США.
Соглашение, достигнутое между владельцами порта и груза, с указанием необходимых мер безопасности.

Gemi Güvenlik Zabiti ve ABD Sahil Güvenliğinin müşterek doldurduğu bir anlaşmadır (kontrol listesi)

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: “安全声明”是什么？ 请选择一个正确答案。

船只安全官和美国海岸警卫队共同完成的协议（检查清单）
港口和货物业主之间的文档，表明所需的安全措施

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: O que é uma "Declaração de proteção"? Selecione UMA resposta correta.

Um acordo (lista de verificação) realizado em conjunto pelo Oficial de proteção do navio e a Guarda Costeira dos EUA
Um documento entre o porto e o proprietário da carga, informando as medidas de proteção exigidas

options: Un acuerdo, en forma de lista de comprobación, entre un buque y unas instalaciones portuarias u otro buque, en el que se especifican las medidas de seguridad que cada parte ha de implementar
Un acuerdo, en forma de lista de comprobación, que han de rellenar el responsable de seguridad del buque y la Guardia Costera estadounidense

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: '보안 선언문'이 무엇입니까? 올바른 답을 하나 선택하십시오.
options: 선박 및 항만 시설이나 다른 배 간의 합의(체크리스트), 각각 구현되는 보안 조치 지정
선박 보안 책임자와 미국 해안경비대 간에 협력 체결한 합의서(체크리스트)
필수 보안 수단으로 시작하는 항만과 화물 소유주 간 문서
배의 보안 수준으로 시작하는 배의 선언문

CD0115 — Security awareness.question: Cos'è una "Dichiarazione di sicurezza"? Selezionare l'UNICA risposta esatta.
options: Un accordo (lista di controllo) tra la nave e un impianto portuale o un'altra nave che specifica le misure di sicurezza da implementare
Un accordo (lista di controllo) raggiunto dall'ufficiale di sicurezza della nave e dalla guardia costiera statunitense
Un documento tra il porto e il proprietario del carico che riporta le misure di sicurezza necessarie
