If there is sufficient sea-room, she should avoid impeding the passage of other vessels navigating in or near any deep-water routes
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: With particular caution having full regard to her special condition

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: When a vessel is in doubt as to whether she is overtaking another vessel, what must she do according to the COLREGs?
options: She shall assume that this is the case and act accordingly
She shall assume that this is not the case and act accordingly
She shall maintain her course and speed
She shall sound one short blast and make a broad alteration of course to starboard
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: She shall assume that this is the case and act accordingly

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: According to Rule 15 “Crossing Situation”, which vessel shall keep out of the way?
options: The vessel which has the other on her own starboard side
The vessel which has the other on her own port side
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: The vessel which has the other on her own starboard side

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessels
options: Power-driven vessel engaged in towing, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light and tow, where length of tow exceeds 200 metres,  towing vessel and tow restricted in their ability to deviate from their course

Power-driven vessel engaged in towing, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, length of tow under 200 metres, towing vessel and tow restricted in their ability to deviate from their course
Power-driven vessel engaged in towing, less than 50 metres in length, where length of tow exceeds 200 metres,  towing vessel and tow restricted in their ability to deviate from their course
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Power-driven vessel engaged in towing, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light and tow, where length of tow exceeds 200 metres,  towing vessel and tow restricted in their ability to deviate from their course

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What whistle signal can a vessel proceeding along a narrow, inland channel and  approaching a bend around a high bluff or headland use to indicate its presence to another vessel which may be out of sight around that bend?
options: One prolonged blast, followed by two short blasts
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: One prolonged blast

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel constrained by her draught, underway
Vessel constrained by her draught, at anchor
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, at anchor
Vessel not under command, at anchor
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel constrained by her draught, underway

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, length unknown,  obstruction to her starboard side
Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, length unknown,  obstruction to her port side
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, length unknown,  obstruction to her starboard side

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, shooting nets

Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, making way through the water, outlying gear extending more than 150 metres horizontally in the direction of the all-round white lights
Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, shooting nets, at anchor
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, shooting nets

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, shooting nets

Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, making way through the water, outlying gear extending more than 150 metres horizontally in the direction of the all-round white lights

Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, hauling nets
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, shooting nets

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: At what distance must outlying gear extend from a fishing vessel for it to be obliged to display an all-round white light or a cone apex upwards in the direction of the gear?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: 150 metres

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Air-cushioned vessel operating in the non-displacement mode, less than 50 metres in length
Wing-in-Ground Vessel, less than 50 metres in length, taking-off, landing or in flight near the surface
Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, not making way through the water, nets fast on an obstruction
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Wing-in-Ground Vessel, less than 50 metres in length, taking-off, landing or in flight near the surface

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: According to Rule 16 “Action by Give-way Vessel” in what way must a vessel take action to keep out of the way?
options: She shall, so far as possible, take early and substantial action to keep well clear
She shall sound one short blast and make a broad alteration of course to starboard
She shall slacken her speed and then take all way off by stopping or reversing her means of propulsion
She shall avoid altering course to port for a vessel on her own port side
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: She shall, so far as possible, take early and substantial action to keep well clear

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Sailing vessel underway, less than 20 metres in length
Sailing vessel making way, less than 50 metres in length
Sailing vessel, length unknown, at anchor
Vessel engaged in fishing, other than trawling, less than 12 metres in length
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Sailing vessel underway, less than 20 metres in length

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel(s)
options: Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling,^Mmore than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, shooting nets

Power-driven vessel engaged in towing, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light and tow, where length of tow under 200 metres, not restricted in their ability to deviate from their course
Power-driven vessel engaged in towing, less than 50 metres in length, length of tow exceeds 200 metres, towing vessel and tow restricted in their ability to deviate from their course
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Power-driven vessel engaged in towing, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light and tow, where length of tow under 200 metres, not restricted in their ability to deviate from their course

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: According to Rule 17, if a stand-on vessel finds herself so close that collision cannot be avoided by the action of the give-way vessel on its own, what must that stand-on vessel do?
options: She shall take such action as will best aid to avoid collision
She must continue to maintain her course and speed in compliance with Rule 17 “Action by Stand-on Vessel”
She shall sound one short blast and make a broad alteration of course to starboard
She must immediately stop and take all way off and in any event avoid passing ahead of the other vessel
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: She shall take such action as will best aid to avoid collision

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel(s)
options: Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, less than 50 metres in length, obstruction to her port side
Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, less than 50 metres in length, obstruction to her starboard side
Vessel engaged in towing alongside, less than 50 metres in length, objects being towed to both sides, restricted in their ability to deviate from their course
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, less than 50 metres in length, obstruction to her port side

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in pilotage duty, underway
Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling
Vessel not under command, at anchor
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in pilotage duty, underway

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What additional whistle signal might this vessel sound to aid identification in conditions of restricted visibility?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Four short blasts

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing the a second masthead light, obstruction to her starboard side

Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing the a second masthead light, obstruction to her port side

Vessel engaged in towing alongside, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing the a second masthead light, objects being towed to both sides, restricted in their ability to deviate from their course
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, making way through the water, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing the a second masthead light, obstruction to her starboard side

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: According to Rule 17, what may a stand-on vessel do, once it becomes apparent to her that a vessel required to keep out of the way is not taking appropriate action in compliance with the Rules?
options: She may take action to avoid collision by her manoeuvre alone
She may disregard the Rules of the Road from that point on
She should take action to avoid collision by alteration of her course and/or speed
She must attempt to contact the other vessel by VHF
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: She may take action to avoid collision by her manoeuvre alone

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Air-cushioned vessel operating in the non-displacement mode, less than 50 metres in length
Wing-in-Ground Vessel, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, taking-off, landing or in flight near the surface

Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, not making way through the water, nets fast on an obstruction
Power-driven vessel underway, engaged in underwater operations
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Wing-in-Ground Vessel, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, taking-off, landing or in flight near the surface

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Power-driven vessel underway but not making way through the water
Sailing vessel underway, but not making way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Sailing vessel underway

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What additional identification signal may be sounded by a pilot vessel “engaged in pilotage duty”?
options: One prolonged blast, followed by three short blasts
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Four short blasts

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What day signal must be displayed by a power-driven vessel engaged in towing, when the length of the tow exceeds 200 metres?
options: A diamond shape, where it can best be seen
A cylinder shape on the foremast
Two black balls where they can best be seen
A cone, apex downwards, in the direction of he tow
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A diamond shape, where it can best be seen

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal?
options: A vessel engaged in underwater operations, about to deploy divers
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel in distress

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing, hauling nets
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel not under command, at anchor
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel aground

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in underwater operations, divers down
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel in distress

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre (other than a vessel engaged in mine clearance operations), not making way through the water
Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, making way through the water, hauling nets
Vessel not under command, at anchor
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre (other than a vessel engaged in mine clearance operations), not making way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in underwater operations, bout to deploy divers
Vessel not under command, at anchor, giving warning signal to approaching vessels
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel in distress

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How many forward masthead lights must be displayed in a vertical line forward on a power-driven vessel engaged in towing, when the length of the tow, measured from the stern of the towing vessel to the after end of the tow, exceeds 200 metres?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Three

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Under which of the following circumstances would you consider yourself an overtaking vessel?
options: When coming up with another vessel from a direction of more than 22.5 degrees abaft her beam, that is, in such a position with reference to the vessel she is overtaking, that at night she would be able to see only the sternlight of that vessel but neither of her sidelights
When approaching from behind another vessel, such that with reference to the vessel she is overtaking, she would see the sternlight at the same time as the appropriate sidelight become visible

When coming up with another vessel from a direction of more than 60 degrees abaft her beam, that is, in such a position with reference to the vessel she is overtaking, that by day, she would see the masts in a line, or nearly in a line
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: When coming up with another vessel from a direction of more than 22.5 degrees abaft her beam, that is, in such a position with reference to the vessel she is overtaking, that at night she would be able to see only the sternlight of that vessel but neither of her sidelights

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What day signal must be displayed by a vessel or object being towed when the tow length exceeds 200 metres, (other than an inconspicuous or partly submerged vessel or object or combination of such vessels or objects)?
options: A diamond shape, where it can best be seen
A black ball, at the fore end of the tow
A black ball, at the aft end of the tow
The International Code signal flag ‘T’ at the aft end of the tow
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A diamond shape, where it can best be seen

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Power-driven vessel, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing the a second masthead light, engaged in towing where tow exceeds than 200 metres in length, being an inconspicuous, partly submerged vessel or object, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre

Power-driven vessel, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing the a second masthead light, engaged in towing where tow is under 200 metres in length, being an inconspicuous, partly submerged vessel or object, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Power-driven vessel, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing the a second masthead light, engaged in towing where tow exceeds than 200 metres in length, being an inconspicuous, partly submerged vessel or object, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing by trawl lines
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel in distress

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Pleasure craft landing passengers by dinghy
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel in distress

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Aircraft carrier, engaged in flying on and off aircraft
Vessel engaged in fishing with purse seine gear
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Submarine, underway

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What term is applied to a partly submerged flexible container used for transporting liquid cargoes?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Dracone

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the definition of a fishing vessel engaged in trawling?
options: One which drags a dredge net or other apparatus used as a fishing appliance through the water
One which displays green and white lights
One where there is outlying gear extending more than 150 metres horizontally from the vessel
One which has been assessed and categorized as capable of operating purse-seine equipment by the appropriate Classification Society
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: One which drags a dredge net or other apparatus used as a fishing appliance through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What alternative arrangement to sidelights and sternlight may be exhibited by a sailing vessel of less than 20 metres in length?
options: A conical shape, apex down, where it can best be seen
Placing the lights close together near the top of the mast
A blue light, where it can best be seen
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A combined lantern

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What does this signal mean?^M- Open water^M- Clear conditions
options: “I am altering my course to port”
“I am altering my course to starboard”
Fog signal of a power-driven vessel
Fog signal of a vessel under 20 metres in length, at anchor
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: “I am altering my course to port”

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel at anchor, seen from starboard side
Vessel at anchor, seen from port side
Vessel engaged in towing alongside, stern-on
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel at anchor, seen from starboard side

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel aground, seen from port side
Vessel aground, seen from starboard side
Vessel engaged in towing alongside, stern-on
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel aground, seen from port side

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What does this signal mean?^M- Open water^M- Clear conditions
options: “I am altering my course to port”
Fog signal of a vessel under 20 metres in length, at anchor
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: “I am operating astern propulsion”

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the arc of visibility of the additional red and green lights exhibited at or near the top of the mast of a sailing vessel?
options: 225º, from right ahead to 22.5º abaft the beam on either side of the vessel
200º, from right ahead to 10º abaft the beam on either side of the vessel
120º, from right astern to 60º on either side of the vessel
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: All round

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the required minimum range for a sidelight on a vessel of 50 metres or more in length?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: 3 miles

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What lights are required on an inconspicuous, partly submerged vessel or object of less than 25 metres in breadth, (other than a dracone) being towed?
options: One all-round white light at or near the forward and one all-round white light at or near the aft end
One all-round yellow light at or near the forward and one all-round yellow light at or near the aft end
One all-round blue light at or near the aft end
Two all-round yellow lights at the extremities of breadth on the aft end
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: One all-round white light at or near the forward and one all-round white light at or near the aft end

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How do the COLREGs explain the term “Underway”?
options: A vessel that is not at anchor, or made fast to the shore, or aground
A vessel that is making way through the water
A vessel that is entitles to exhibit sidelights and a sternlight, or by day the equivalent shapes where they can best be seen
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel that is not at anchor, or made fast to the shore, or aground

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What additional whistle signal might a vessel at anchor sound in restricted visibility, to give warning of her presence to an approaching vessel?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: The code letter “R”

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal? ^M- (Repeated - not more than 1 minute interval)^M- In or near an area of restricted visibility
options: A vessel at anchor, more than 100 metres in length
A vessel at anchor, more than 50 metres in length
A vessel at anchor, more than 20 metres in length
A vessel engaged in mine-clearance operations, at anchor
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel at anchor, more than 100 metres in length

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, length unknown, at anchor, no obstructions exist on either side of the vessel
Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, length unknown, not making way, obstructions on both sides of the vessel
Power-driven vessel, less than 50 metres in length, engaged in towing alongside to both sides, tug and tow restricted in their ability to deviate from their course
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, length unknown, at anchor, no obstructions exist on either side of the vessel

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel displaying signal requesting a pilot
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel at anchor

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How do the COLREGs define “Restricted Visibility”?
options: Fog, mist, heavy precipitation and sandstorms
Rain, drizzle, hail or snow falling heavily enough to restrict visibility
Any condition in which visibility is restricted by fog, mist, falling snow, heavy rainstorms, sandstorms or any other similar causes
Any condition in which visibility is reduced to less than a ship’s length by fog, mist, falling snow, heavy rainstorms, dust, smog or other similar causes
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Any condition in which visibility is restricted by fog, mist, falling snow, heavy rainstorms, sandstorms or any other similar causes

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the required minimum range for a masthead light on a vessel of 50 metres or more in length?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: 6 miles

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Which Annex to the Rules lists the “Distress Signals”?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Annex IV

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How should a vessel maintain a look-out, as identified in Rule 5: “Look-out”?
options: By sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision

By visual and aural means, as well as by any other applicable electronic means possible in the prevailing circumstances and conditions, so as to make a reasonable appraisal of the situation and decide if there might be a risk of collision
By all possible means, including radar, ARPA, VHF and AIS to establish if there is a risk of collision
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: By sight and hearing as well as by all available means appropriate in the prevailing circumstances and conditions so as to make a full appraisal of the situation and of the risk of collision

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How does Rule 3 “Definitions” describe a “Sailing Vessel”?
options: Any vessel under sail provided that propelling machinery, if fitted, is not being used
Any vessel fitted with sails as the principal form of propulsion power
Every vessel registered with an authorized sailing club, society or similar organization
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Any vessel under sail provided that propelling machinery, if fitted, is not being used

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What does a vessel under sail exhibit to indicate that it is also being propelled by machinery?
options: A conical shape, apex down, where it can best be seen
A conical shape, apex upwards, in the fore part of the vessel
A cylindrical shape, where it can best be seen
A diamond shape, at the mainmast head
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A conical shape, apex down, where it can best be seen

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What does this signal mean?^M- Narrow channel^M- Clear conditions^M- Vessel in sight
options: “I intend to overtake you on your port side”
“I intend to overtake you on your starboard side”
“I am engaged in embarking / disembarking my pilot”
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: “I intend to overtake you on your port side”

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal? ^M- (Repeated - not more than 1 minute interval)^M- In or near an area of restricted visibility
options: A vessel aground, less than 100 metres in length
A vessel at anchor, more than 100 metres in length
A vessel at anchor, less than 100 metres in length
A vessel aground, more than 100 metres in length
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel aground, less than 100 metres in length

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What length is the vessel making this signal? ^M- (Repeated - not more than 1 minute interval)^M- In or near an area of restricted visibility
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Less than 100 metres

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal? ^M- (Repeated - not more than 2 minute interval)^M- In or near an area of restricted visibility
options: A power-driven vessel, stopped and making no way through the water
A power-driven vessel, making way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A power-driven vessel, stopped and making no way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What does this signal mean?^M- Narrow channel^M- Clear conditions^M- Vessel in sight
options: “I intend to overtake you on your starboard side”
“I intend to overtake you on your port side”
“I am engaged in changing my pilot”
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: “I intend to overtake you on your starboard side”

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: When will a power-driven vessel engaged in pushing and a vessel being pushed be considered as simply a “power-driven vessel”?
options: When they are rigidly connected as a composite unit
When both the vessel engaged in pushing and the vessel being pushed have independent propulsion machinery
When the vessel being pushed is shorter in length than the vessel pushing
When they are not considered to be restricted in their ability to manoeuvre
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: When they are rigidly connected as a composite unit

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How does Rule 3 “Definitions” describe a “Vessel Not Under Command?
options: A vessel which through some exceptional circumstance is unable to manoeuvre as required by these Rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel
A vessel which from the nature of her work is restricted in her ability to manoeuvre as required by these Rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel
A vessel which through a listed technical clause applied by the relevant Classification Society is exempt from manoeuvring in compliance with the International Collision Regulations
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel which through some exceptional circumstance is unable to manoeuvre as required by these Rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the “safe distance” around a vessel engaged in mine clearance operations as defined by the Rules?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: 1000 metres

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: If whistles are fitted on a vessel at a distance apart of more than 100 metres, how will manoeuvring and warning signals be given?
options: On the forward whistle first, then the after whistle immediately afterwards
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: On one whistle only

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How does Rule 3 “Definitions” describe a “Vessel Constrained by her Draught?
options: A vessel which because of her draught in relation to the available depth and width of navigable water is severely restricted in her ability to deviate from the course she is following
A vessel which because she has a deeper draught than the vessels around her has right of way

A vessel which because of her draught in relation to the surrounding depth and length of the navigable channel in which she is proceeding is likely to be restricted in her ability to deviate from the course she is following
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel which because of her draught in relation to the available depth and width of navigable water is severely restricted in her ability to deviate from the course she is following

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the fog signal for a vessel aground, 150 metres in length?
options: At not more than 1 minute intervals: 3 strokes on bell forward, rapid ringing of the bell for about 5 seconds, 3 strokes on the bell, sounding gong aft for about 5 seconds
At not more than 2 minute intervals: 5 strokes on bell forward, rapid ringing of the bell for about 5 seconds, 5 strokes on the bell, sounding gong aft for about 5 seconds
At not more than 1 minute intervals: 5 strokes on bell forward, rapid ringing of the bell for about 5 seconds, 5 strokes on the bell, sounding gong aft for about 10 seconds
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: At not more than 1 minute intervals: 3 strokes on bell forward, rapid ringing of the bell for about 5 seconds, 3 strokes on the bell, sounding gong aft for about 5 seconds

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Is a power-driven vessel underway, of less than 50 metres in length, obliged to exhibit a second masthead light?
options: No, but may do so by Rule 23: “Power-driven Vessels Underway”
Yes, but only in the vicinity of a narrow channel or fairway
No, but may be required to do so in compliance with Rule 27 “Vessels Not Under Command or Restricted in their Ability to Manoeuvre”
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: No, but may do so by Rule 23: “Power-driven Vessels Underway”

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal? ^M- (Immediately after a sound signal comprising one prolonged blast plus two short blasts)^M- In or near an area of restricted visibility
options: A vessel being towed, if manned
The last vessel in a series of vessels in a single tow, if manned
A vessel indicating that an earlier signal is to be disregarded
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel being towed, if manned

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal? ^M- (Repeated - not more than 1 minute interval)^M- In or near an area of restricted visibility
options: A vessel at anchor, less than 100 metres in length
A vessel at anchor, more than 100 metres in length
A vessel at anchor, less than 12 metres in length
A vessel engaged in underwater operations, at anchor
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel at anchor, less than 100 metres in length

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What additional whistle signal might a vessel aground sound in restricted visibility, to give warning of her presence to an approaching vessel?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: The code letter “U”

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: In order for a Wing-in-Ground craft to exhibit a high intensity all-round flashing red light in compliance with the Rules, what must she be doing?
options: Taking-off, landing and in flight near the surface
Navigating as a power-driven vessel underway, but restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Taking-off, landing and in flight near the surface

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: When in open waters and in sight of one another, what whistle signal should a power-driven vessel underway make to indicate that she is altering her course to starboard?
options: One prolonged blast, followed by two short blasts
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: One short blast

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How does Rule 3 “Definitions” describe a “Vessel Restricted in her Ability to Manoeuvre?
options: A vessel which from the nature of her work is restricted in her ability to manoeuvre as required by these Rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel
A vessel which through some exceptional circumstance is unable to manoeuvre as required by these Rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel
A vessel which through a listed technical clause applied by the relevant Classification Society is exempt from manoeuvring in compliance with the International Collision Regulations
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel which from the nature of her work is restricted in her ability to manoeuvre as required by these Rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Can Traffic Separation Schemes created by a Government or State be adopted by the International Maritime Organization for the purpose of the COLREGs?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Yes

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the fog signal of a vessel “Restricted in her Ability to Manoeuvre”?
options: At not more than 2 minute intervals, one short blast
At not more than 1 minute intervals, two short blasts
At not more than 2 minute intervals, one prolonged blast
At not more than 2 minute intervals, one prolonged blast, followed by two short blasts
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: At not more than 2 minute intervals, one prolonged blast, followed by two short blasts

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the arc of visibility for a masthead light, as described in Rule 21: Definitions?
options: 225º, from right ahead to 22.5º abaft the beam on either side of the vessel
200º, from right ahead to 10º abaft the beam on either side of the vessel
180º, from right ahead to directly on the beam on either side of the vessel
250º, from right ahead to 35º abaft the beam on either side of the vessel
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: 225º, from right ahead to 22.5º abaft the beam on either side of the vessel

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal? ^M- (Repeated - at 1 minute intervals)
options: A vessel engaged in underwater operations,^Mabout to deploy divers
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A vessel in distress

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal?^M- (Repeated - not more than 2 minute interval)^M- Open water^M- In or near an area of restricted visibility
options: A pilot vessel engaged in pilotage duty, less^Mthan 100 metres in length, at anchor
A sailing vessel, making way through the water
A vessel engaged in underwater operations,^Mstopped and making no way through the water
A pilot vessel, engaged in pilotage duty, more^Mthan 100 metres in length, stopped and making^Mno way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A pilot vessel engaged in pilotage duty, less^Mthan 100 metres in length, at anchor

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: When a power-driven vessel is stopped and making no way through the water, what would her fog signal be?
options: At not more than 2 minute intervals, two prolonged blasts, with about 2 seconds between them
At not more than 1 minute intervals, two short blasts, with about three seconds between them
At not more than 2 minute intervals, one prolonged blast
At not more than 2 minute intervals, one prolonged blast, followed by two short blasts
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: At not more than 2 minute intervals, two prolonged blasts, with about 2 seconds between them

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Which of the following is a statement extracted from the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea?
options: Any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof shall be exonerated from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or neglecting any precautions normally taken by seamen, or by any special circumstances applicable in the case

Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case

Nothing in these Rules shall benefit the vessel, her owner, master or crew from any arrangement whereby commercial considerations can be brought to bear over precautions that might normally be applied by seamen, or by the special circumstances of a case
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Nothing in these Rules shall exonerate any vessel, or the owner, master or crew thereof, from the consequences of any neglect to comply with these Rules or the neglect of any precaution which may be required by the ordinary practice of seamen, or by the special circumstances of the case

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: When in open waters and in sight of one another, what whistle signal should a power-driven vessel underway make to indicate that she is altering her course to port?
options: One prolonged blast, followed by two short blasts
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Two short blasts

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Which Annex to the Rules lists the “Positioning and Technical Details of Lights and Shapes”?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Annex I

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the arc of visibility for a sidelight, as described in Rule 21: Definitions?
options: 225º, from right ahead to 22.5º abaft the beam on either side of the vessel
112.5º, from right ahead to 22.5º abaft the beam on the respective side of the vessel
100º, from right ahead to 10º abaft the beam on the respective side of the vessel
120º, from right ahead to 20º abaft the beam on the respective side of the vessel
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: 112.5º, from right ahead to 22.5º abaft the beam on the respective side of the vessel

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What does this signal mean?^M- Narrow channel^M- Clear conditions^M- Vessel in sight
options: “I intend to overtake you on your port side”
“I intend to overtake you on your starboard side”
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: “I agree to your overtaking manoeuvre”

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal? ^M- (Repeated - not more than 2 minute interval)^M- Open water^M- In or near an area of restricted visibility
options: A pilot vessel engaged in pilotage duty,^Mmaking way through the water
A sailing vessel making way ^Mthrough the water
A vessel engaged in underwater operations,^Mstopped and making no way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A pilot vessel engaged in pilotage duty,^Mmaking way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in underwater operations, about to deploy sonar
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel in distress

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in underwater operations, about to deploy divers
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel in distress

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What vessel makes this signal? ^M- (Repeated - not more than 2 minute interval)^M- Open water^M- In or near an area of restricted visibility
options: A pilot vessel, engaged in pilotage duty,^Mstopped and making no way through the water
A sailing vessel, making way through the water
A vessel engaged in underwater operations,^Mstopped and making no way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: A pilot vessel, engaged in pilotage duty,^Mstopped and making no way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the frequency of a “flashing light”, as defined in Rule 21: Definitions?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: 120 flashes or more per minute

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Which Annex to the Rules lists the “Additional Signals for Fishing Vessels Fishing in Close Proximity”?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Annex II

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the duration of a “prolonged” blast as defined in the COLREGs?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: 4-6 seconds

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing with purse seine gear, length unknown,  making way through the water and hampered by its gear
Vessel engaged in pilotage duty, deploying pilot launch
Vessel engaged in fishing, other than trawling, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, shooting nets
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing with purse seine gear, length unknown,  making way through the water and hampered by its gear

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing, other than trawling
Sailing vessel, being propelled by machinery
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Sailing vessel underway

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What does Rule 8 “Action to Avoid Collision” recommend as potentially the most effective action to avoid a close-quarters situation?
options: Alteration of course alone, provided that it is made in good time, is substantial and does not result in another close-quarters situation
Alteration of course and/or speed, provided that it is made in ample time, at an adequate distance and does not result in increasing the risk of collision with a vessel on the port side
Alteration of course alone, provided that an alteration to course to port for a vessel forward of the beam is avoided
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Alteration of course alone, provided that it is made in good time, is substantial and does not result in another close-quarters situation

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: (Other than a vessel en route to or from a port, installation, structure or pilot station within an inshore traffic zone or for the purposes of avoiding immediate danger) what length of vessel is permitted to use an inshore traffic zone, even if adjacent to a traffic separation scheme?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Less than 20 metres

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, not making way through the water
Vessel engaged in towing, length of tow unknown

Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, making way through the water, outlying gear extending more than 150 metres horizontally in the direction of the all-round white light
Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, making way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, not making way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, not making way through the water, nets fast on an obstruction

Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, more than 20 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, not making way through the water, nets fast on an obstruction
Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, not making way through the water, shooting nets
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, not making way through the water, nets fast on an obstruction

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, not making way through the water, nets fast on an obstruction

Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, not making way through the water, nets fast on an obstruction
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, not making way through the water, nets fast on an obstruction

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: A vessel is permitted to engage in fishing within a traffic lane but what obligations does that vessel have to other vessels proceeding within that traffic lane?
options: The fishing vessel shall not impede the passage of any vessel following a traffic lane
The fishing vessel shall not use outlying gear horizontally over a distance of more than 150 metres
The fishing vessel shall only manoeuvre in accordance with the applicable special rules made by the appropriate authority for the roadsteads, channels  and fairways connected to the traffic lane
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: The fishing vessel shall not impede the passage of any vessel following a traffic lane

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How do the Rules describe “any alteration of course and/or speed to avoid collision”?
options: Any alteration of course and/or speed to avoid collision shall, if the circumstances of the case admit, be large enough to be readily apparent to another vessel observing visually or by radar; a succession of small alterations of course and/or speed should be avoided

Any alteration of course and/or speed to avoid collision shall be made in accordance with special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected to the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels; a series of alterations that may not be readily apparent to another vessel should be avoided

Any alterations of course and/or speed to avoid collision shall, if possible in the prevailing circumstances and conditions, be such as to minimize any deviation from the track indicated in the vessel’s passage plan
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Any alteration of course and/or speed to avoid collision shall, if the circumstances of the case admit, be large enough to be readily apparent to another vessel observing visually or by radar; a succession of small alterations of course and/or speed should be avoided

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing, gear extending 150 metres horizontally in the direction of the white light
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Sailing vessel underway

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing with purse seine gear, length unknown,  making way through the water and hampered by its gear
Vessel engaged in pilotage duty, deploying pilot launch
Vessel engaged in fishing, other than trawling, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, at anchor, shooting nets
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing with purse seine gear, length unknown,  making way through the water and hampered by its gear

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing, gear extending 150 metres horizontally in the direction of the white light
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Sailing vessel underway

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel not under command, length unknown, not making way through the water
Vessel not under command, length unknown, making way through the water
Vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, length unknown, underway
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel not under command, length unknown, not making way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What is the fog signal of a vessel “Constrained by her Draught”?
options: At not more than 2 minute intervals, one short blast
At not more than 1 minute intervals, two short blasts
At not more than 2 minute intervals, one prolonged blast
At not more than 2 minute intervals, one prolonged blast, followed by two short blasts
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: At not more than 2 minute intervals, one prolonged blast, followed by two short blasts

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: In terms of “Risk of Collision”, what do the Rules say about “scanty radar information”?
options: Assumptions shall not be made on the basis of scanty information, especially scanty radar information
Conclusions must not be drawn from scanty radar information that may have been used in an automatic radar plot
Actions taken to avoid collision shall be carefully monitored until all risk of danger is past, particularly when such actions are based on scanty radar information
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Assumptions shall not be made on the basis of scanty information, especially scanty radar information

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in pilotage duty, at anchor, exhibiting identification signal
Vessel engaged in pilotage duty, underway, exhibiting identification signal
Vessel not under command, at anchor, exhibiting warning signal to approaching vessels
Sailing vessel underway, using propelling machinery
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in pilotage duty, at anchor, exhibiting identification signal

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, hauling nets

Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, shooting nets

Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, nets fast on an obstruction
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, hauling nets

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, making way through the water
Vessel engaged in fishing, hauling nets
Vessel engaged in fishing, shooting nets
Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, less than 50 metres in length, making way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, making way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, making way through the water
Vessel engaged in fishing, at anchor
Power-driven vessel underway, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, less than 50 metres in length, making way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, making way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, hauling nets

Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, shooting nets

Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, nets fast on an obstruction
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length, or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, hauling nets

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How do the Rules describe “any action to avoid collision”?
options: Any action to avoid collision shall be taken in accordance with the Rules of this Part and shall, if the circumstances of the case admit, be positive, made in ample time and with due regard to the observance of good seamanship

Any action to avoid collision shall be taken in accordance with special rules made by an appropriate authority for roadsteads, harbours, rivers, lakes or inland waterways connected to the high seas and navigable by seagoing vessels
Any action to avoid collision shall be made in accordance with any special rules made by the Government of any State with respect to close-quarters situations in waters within their jurisdiction
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Any action to avoid collision shall be taken in accordance with the Rules of this Part and shall, if the circumstances of the case admit, be positive, made in ample time and with due regard to the observance of good seamanship

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: What whistle signal would you use to indicate to another vessel in sight that you had put your engines astern?
options: One prolonged blast, followed by two short blasts
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Three short blasts

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel(s)
options: Power-driven vessel, length unknown, engaged in towing where length of tow exceeds 200 metres, towing vessel and tow restricted in their ability to deviate from their course
Power-driven vessel, length unknown, engaged in towing a dracone, less than 25 metres in breadth, towing vessel and tow restricted in their ability to deviate from their course
Power-driven vessel, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, at anchor
Power-driven vessel, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, engaged in underwater operations
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Power-driven vessel, length unknown, engaged in towing where length of tow exceeds 200 metres, towing vessel and tow restricted in their ability to deviate from their course

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel not under command, length unknown, making way through the water
Vessel constrained by her draught, length unknown, underway
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel not under command, length unknown, making way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How far does the gear extend horizontally from this fishing vessel?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: More than 150 metres

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessels
options: Vessels engaged in fishing (pair-trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length,  or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, hauling nets
Vessels engaged in fishing (pair-trawling), more than 50 metres in length,  making way through the water, hauling nets
Vessels engaged in fishing (pair-trawling), more than 50 metres, making way through the water, shooting nets
Power-driven vessel engaged in towing, where each vessel is illuminating the other for the purposes of safety
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessels engaged in fishing (pair-trawling), more than 20 metres but less than 50 metres in length,  or less than 20 metres in length and showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water, hauling nets

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: You are in open water in clear visibility and you meet a vessel on a reciprocal course.  What action would you reasonably expect the other vessel to take?
options: To alter her course to starboard in compliance with Rule 14
To alter her course to port in compliance with Rule 15
To make contact to discuss a suitable manoeuvre
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: To alter her course to starboard in compliance with Rule 14

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: According to Rule 8 “Action to Avoid Collision”, what action should you take if you need more time to assess a developing close-quarters situation?
options: Slacken your speed or take all way off by stopping or reversing your means of propulsion
Sound one short blast and make a broad alteration of course to starboard
Attempt to make contact with the other vessel by VHF
Use the signalling lamp to transmit the code letter “U”, thereby indicating to the other vessel that you request they slacken their speed
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Slacken your speed or take all way off by stopping or reversing your means of propulsion

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Power-driven vessel underway, less than 50 metres in length
Power-driven vessel underway, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing the a second masthead light
Vessel at anchor, over 100 metres in length
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Power-driven vessel underway, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing the a second masthead light

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing, length unknown
Vessel engaged in fishing, outlying gear extending more than 150 metres horizontally in the direction of the cone shapes
Power-driven vessel underway, restricted in her ability to manoeuvre
Vessel constrained by her draught, underway
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing, length unknown

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in mine clearance operations, underway, less than 50 metres in length
Vessel engaged in dredging or underwater operations, underway, no  obstruction exists on either side of the vessel
Vessel engaged on convoy duties, making way through the water
Vessel engaged in mine clearance operations, underway, more  than 50 metres in length
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in mine clearance operations, underway, less than 50 metres in length

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: At what minimum safe distance should you pass this vessel?
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: 1000 metres

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessel
options: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), length unknown, not making way through the water
Vessel engaged in fishing, at anchor
Vessel engaged in fishing other than trawling, less than 50 metres in length, making way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessel engaged in fishing (trawling), length unknown, not making way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: Identify the vessels
options: Vessels engaged in fishing (pair-trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water

Vessel engaged in fishing with purse-seine equipment, more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Vessels engaged in fishing (pair-trawling), more than 50 metres in length, or less than 50 metres in length and showing a second masthead light, or less than 20 metres in length and also showing the additional signals voluntarily, making way through the water

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How effective must any action taken to avoid collision be, according to Rule 8 “Action to Avoid Collision”?
options: Such as to result in passing at a safe distance
It must result in a minimum closest approach of at least 0.5 mile
Such that a close-quarters situation is also avoided
Adequate enough to permit both vessels to continue to observe successfully by radar until all danger is past and clear
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Such as to result in passing at a safe distance

CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.question: How do the Regulations say a vessel should proceed in terms of “speed”?
options: Every vessel shall at all times proceed at a safe speed so that she can take proper and effective action to avoid collision and be stopped within a distance appropriate to the prevailing circumstances and conditions
Every vessel shall when possible proceed at a speed adapted to the prevailing circumstances and conditions, so as to minimize the deviation from her charter speed and schedule
Every vessel shall at all times proceed at the speed listed in a vessel’s Passage Plan and authorized by the Master
CD0172 — International Collision Regulat.answer: Every vessel shall at all times proceed at a safe speed so that she can take proper and effective action to avoid collision and be stopped within a distance appropriate to the prevailing circumstances and conditions
