The ash content of a fuel is limited according to the ISO 8217 fuel tables. Which one of the following is the highest risk when operating an engine on fuel with a high ash content?
options: Risk of abrasive damage to injection equipment and cylinder components.
Risk of fuel system filter blockage.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Risk of abrasive damage to injection equipment and cylinder components.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which of the following options is the best description of marine diesel oil?
options: Mainly distillate fuel with a small proportion of heavy fuel.
Mainly residual fuel with a small proportion of distillate fuel.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Mainly distillate fuel with a small proportion of heavy fuel.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which of the following non-hydrocarbon elements found in marine residual fuels is the most likely to originate from part of the refining process?
A value for fuel viscosity is required for a number of operational reasons. Select all of the operations for which a viscosity value for the fuel is required from the options given.
options: Calculating storage temperatures to ensure transfer of fuel is possible.
Calculating the quantity of the fuel onboard.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Calculating storage temperatures to ensure transfer of fuel is possible.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Aluminium and silicon may be present in the fuel. What is the most likely source of these contaminants?
Limits for Micro Carbon Residue, MCR, are included in both of the ISO 8217 fuel tables. Which of the following is the best description of the effect of a high value of MCR?
options: Heavy fouling of engine cylinder and exhaust system may occur in the event of poor combustion conditions.
Blockage of fuel oil filters may occur.
Seizure of injection system may occur.
Frequent cleaning of purifiers will be required.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Heavy fouling of engine cylinder and exhaust system may occur in the event of poor combustion conditions.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which one of the following chemical elements is the most likely to increase the risk of high temperature corrosion when present with vanadium during combustion of fuel oil?
Soluble contaminants such as vanadium may be present in residual fuel. What can be done to remove such contaminants from the fuel prior to onboard use?  ^MSelect the ONE correct answer.
options: Fuel soluble contaminants cannot be removed.
Fuel soluble contaminants can be removed in the settling tank.
Fuel soluble contaminants can be removed by filtration.
Fuel soluble contaminants can be removed by centrifuging.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Fuel soluble contaminants cannot be removed.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Although the stability of a fuel is important the ISO 8217 standard tables do not include any absolute stability indicators. Which of the following statements gives the best description of a stable fuel?
options: A stable fuel is one which remains in its original condition during storage and handling under varying conditions.
A stable fuel is one which can be mixed with other fuels.
A stable fuel is one with only one component.
A stable fuel is one which contains no other elements other than hydrogen and carbon.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: A stable fuel is one which remains in its original condition during storage and handling under varying conditions.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which of the following is the best description of the alkane or paraffinic group of hydrocarbon compounds?
options: Saturated hydrocarbon molecules with a straight chain structure.
Unsaturated hydrocarbon molecules with a straight chain structure.
Saturated hydrocarbon molecules with a ring structure.
Unsaturated hydrocarbon molecules with a ring structure.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Saturated hydrocarbon molecules with a straight chain structure.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: The compatibility of one fuel with another cannot be measured directly and may lead to an unstable mixture. To avoid compatibility problems, which of the following options is recommended?
options: If mixing of different fuels cannot be avoided then mix new bunkers with the minimum quantity of old bunkers possible.
If mixing of different fuels cannot be avoided then mix new bunkers with the equal quantities of old bunkers.
If mixing of fuels cannot be avoided then the mixture should be kept in storage for a long period of time to check for problems.
If mixing of different fuels cannot be avoided then mix all of the new bunkers with all of old bunkers remaining onboard.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: If mixing of different fuels cannot be avoided then mix new bunkers with the minimum quantity of old bunkers possible.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which of the following temperature limits is included in the ISO 8217 standard because of safety reasons?
Which of the following can be used to check that the fuel delivered exactly meets the specification of the fuel ordered?
Which of the following temperature ranges is the most likely to be employed for preheating the crude oil for the atmospheric distillation process.
In oil refining the term ‘cracking’ is applied to a process based on which one of the following?
options: The breakdown of heavy hydrocarbons using either heat or heat and chemical means.
Removal of salt and water from the crude.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: The breakdown of heavy hydrocarbons using either heat or heat and chemical means.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which of the following statements is the most accurate with reference to the term ‘combustion quality’?
options: The combustion quality of a fuel refers to how easily the fuel burns once it has been ignited.
The combustion quality of a fuel refers to how easily the fuel can be ignited.
Combustion quality and ignition quality of a fuel are the same thing.
Combustion quality of a fuel depends on the pre-treatment before use.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: The combustion quality of a fuel refers to how easily the fuel burns once it has been ignited.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Although an energy equivalent indicator is not included within the ISO 8217 fuel standard tables it is still an important indication of a fuels quality. Which of the following range of energy levels is most representative of marine fuels?
The best way to remove residual fuel oil from the skin is to wash with clean distillate fuel. True or False?
Which of the following is not a fossil fuel?
If a person swallows a quantity of fuel which of the following actions should be taken?
options: Move the victim to an area where fresh air is present.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which of the following quality indicators is included in the ISO 8217 tables?
options: An ignition quality indicator for distillate fuels.
An ignition quality indicator for residual fuels.
A combustion quality indicator for distillate fuels.
A combustion quality indicator for residual fuels.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: An ignition quality indicator for distillate fuels.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Information regarding the health hazards associated with different materials, including marine fuels, should be obtained before handling and working with the materials. Where would be the most likely source of this information?
Total sediment (potential) is a measure of which of the following?
options: Deposit of sediment due to storage of fuel over a period of time at elevated temperatures.
Deposit of sediment due to mixing with other fuels.
Deposit of sediment due to suspended solids.
Deposit of sediment due to poor combustion.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Deposit of sediment due to storage of fuel over a period of time at elevated temperatures.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which of the following processes allows the chemical energy in fuel oil to be converted into mechanical work?

Operating a diesel engine on fuel oil containing used lubricating oil may result in engine damage due to high levels of debris or remaining additives it may contain. Which of the following options is recognised as an indication of used lubricating oil being present in fuel?
options: Zinc, calcium and phosphorus levels all above limit values.
Zinc, calcium and lead levels above limit values.
Copper, calcium and phosphorus levels above limit values.
Zinc, copper and phosphorus present but levels below limit values.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Zinc, calcium and phosphorus levels all above limit values.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: When testing diesel engine fuel injectors care must be taken to avoid direct skin contact with the high pressure fuel spray. From the options given select the ONE most likely effect on health that may result from this particular hazard.
options: Blood poisoning due to penetration of the skin by fuel.
Cancer due to prolonged or repeated contact.
Dermatitis due to prolonged or repeated contact.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Blood poisoning due to penetration of the skin by fuel.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: When a fuel is described as being incompatible it means that it cannot be mixed with another fuel and remain stable. True or False?
The cetane number is a reliable ignition quality indicator for all marine fuels. True or false?
Which of the following are the parameters used to calculate the CCAI value of a fuel.
Which of the following is the normal gross calorific value of marine residual fuel?
Which of the following outcomes is the most likely as a result of combustion of fuel containing sulphur?
options: Cold corrosion of components may occur.
Hot corrosion of components may occur.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Cold corrosion of components may occur.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: The tables in ISO 8217 cover all of the quality aspects relating to marine fuels. True or False?
Which of the following is the correct meaning of 'Lubricity?
Which one of the following options is the best way to minimise the sodium levels in fuel and so minimise the risk of hot corrosion?
options: Set up centrifuges to operate as clarifiers.
Avoid using fuel with a very low sulphur content.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: The flash point indicates which of the following?
options: The temperature at which a fuel produces vapour which can be ignited by an external ignition source.
The temperature at which a fuel will spontaneously ignite.
The pressure at which a fuel will vaporise.
The temperature at which the fuel will stop flowing.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: The temperature at which a fuel produces vapour which can be ignited by an external ignition source.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Marine residual fuel oil is classed as a distillate fuel. True or False?
Complete the following statement. Marine diesel fuel usually consists of ...
options: hydrocarbon molecules with less than 10 carbon atoms.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: What does the term ‘saturated’ mean when used to describe hydrocarbon molecules?
options: That the atoms are joined together with single bonds.
That the oil has high water content.
That there are more carbon than hydrogen atoms in the molecule.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: That the atoms are joined together with single bonds.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which of the following best describes the aromatic group of hydrocarbons?
options: Hydrocarbon molecules with at least one benzene ring.
Hydrocarbon molecules which are simple chains.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: Hydrocarbon molecules with at least one benzene ring.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Select the best option to complete the following statement: To remove as much catalytic fines as possible from residual fuel you should ...?
options: use low throughput rates on the purifier and fine filters.
increase the quantity of fuel additives.
CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.answer: use low throughput rates on the purifier and fine filters.

CD0179 — Marine Fuel Properties II.question: Which one of the following options is most likely to contaminate fuel oil during the refining process?
Vanadium can be removed from residual marine fuel by filtration. True or False?

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>What is a risk mitigation and contingency plan in relation to ^MSTS (ship to ship) transfer operation?
options: It is a product of all STS requirements.
It is the basis for a risk assessment.
It is a product of a risk assessment.
It is a guide line for emergency planning.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: It is a product of a risk assessment.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>In relation to STS (ship to ship) transfer operations who should fill in the ^MSTS Check List no. 1?
options: The person in overall advisory control.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Ship Owners/Operators.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Whenever possible STS (ship to ship) transfer operations should be carried ^Mout in daylight conditions, If, however, it is decided to carry out such ^Moperations at night which one of the given options is required in order to^Mmake such operation acceptable?
options: Personnel involved must have suitable experience in night STS transfer operations and all parties must agree.
An additional STS Superintendent must be employed.
Transfer must be carried out with both ships underway.
Tug boat assistance must be made available.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Personnel involved must have suitable experience in night STS transfer operations and all parties must agree.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Which daylight signal is required to be hoisted during the ^MSTS (ship to ship) transfer operations?
options: Two black balls with a diamond shape in the middle.
Two diamond shapes with a black ball in the middle.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Two black balls with a diamond shape in the middle.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>When an STS (ship to ship) transfer operation is planned who is responsible ^Mfor informing the local authority?
options: The person in overall advisory control.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: The master of each ship.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>According to the requirements contained in, the MARPOL Annex I – STS Plan,^M– the national  and local authorities should be notified prior ^Mto the commencement of an STS (ship to ship) transfer operation. How ^Mmuch notice is required for such an operation?
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: 48 hours

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>In relation to STS (ship to ship) transfer operations, when should the STS ^Mcheck list no. 2 be completed and confirmed?
options: At the same time as check list no. 1 is confirmed completed.
When operations are underway but before mooring commences.
When the service provider is ready.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Before operations commences.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Select the option which best describes the type of communication which is^M recommended between the two ships during STS (ship to ship) transfer operation?
options: Intrinsically safe VHF/UHF plus visual/voice contact .
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Intrinsically safe VHF/UHF plus visual/voice contact .

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>What should be the first action to be taken if a cargo leakage or spill is ^Mobserved during an STS (ship to ship) transfer operation?
options: Report to the officer in charge in order to stop the transfer in a controlled manner.
Activate the emergency shut-down system tp immediately stop the transfer.
Inform the Master for his permission to stop the transfer.
Activate the emergency alarm system to notify all personnel.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Report to the officer in charge in order to stop the transfer in a controlled manner.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>In relation to STS (ship to ship) transfer operations, which of the given ^Moptions identifies a common feature that is required for both a dedicated ^Mship and an established ship?
options: Both must be equipped with dedicated hose handling gear.
Both must be contracted for a period in a specific location.
Both must be equipped to secure all STS equipment safely for ocean passages.
Both must have an experienced crew.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Both must have an experienced crew.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Which one of the actions given in the options should be taken^Mif communication is lost during an STS (ship to ship) transfer operation?
options: Continue the operation at a reduced pumping rate and establish voice communication at the manifold.
Continue the operation at a reduced pumping rate until normal communication is re-established.
Sound the emergency signal and suspend all operations if safe to do so. Transfer operations should not be resumed until communication is restored.
Reduce pumping rate and inform the Master and the person in overall advisory control of the problem.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Sound the emergency signal and suspend all operations if safe to do so. Transfer operations should not be resumed until communication is restored.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Which factor would have a vital influence on the unmooring operation^Mfollowing an STS (ship to ship) transfer operation with one ship at anchor.
options: An acceptable but strong wind from port side
The difference in the two ship’s displacement
The hydrodynamic interaction caused by underwater hull shapes
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: A change of tide

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>When berthing alongside an anchored ship, inpreparation for an ^MSTS (ship to ship) transfer operation, which ship will normally ^Mdeploy the lines?
options: The anchored ship deploys the first line, the manoeuvring ship deploys the remaining
Both ships deploy equal number of lines
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: The manoeuvring ship

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Who is normally “the person in overall advisory control” of an ^MSTS (ship to ship) transfer operation?
options: An STS Superintendent or one of the ship's Masters.
The pilot , if a pilot is used.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: An STS Superintendent or one of the ship's Masters.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Who is responsible for the STS (ship to ship) transfer operation?
options: The Superintendent in overall advisory control.
Each master is responsible for his ship.
The master on the manoeuvring ship.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Each master is responsible for his ship.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>When two ships are manoeuvring alongside underway, in preparation for an ^MSTS (ship to ship) transfer operation, what is the main reason for securing ^Mthe forward head- and spring lines first?
options: To avoid misalignment of the two ship’s manifolds
Because the first touch on the fenders will always push the ships' bows apart
Because the interaction between the ships will push the smaller ship away
Because the forward motion of the ships driving the water between ^Mthem can push the bows apart
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Because the forward motion of the ships driving the water between ^Mthem can push the bows apart

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Select the option which best describes the preferred procedure to adopt ^Mwhen unmooring and un-berthing following an STS (ship to ship) transfer ^Moperation carried out with both vessels under way.
options: Keep the wind and sea on the port side when unmooring, then bring the two ships ^Mto head into the wind in order to spread them apart
Keep wind and sea on the starboard while unmooring, then bring the wind^Min from astern in order to split the two ships
Keep sea and wind dead ahead throughout the entire operation
Keep the wind and sea abreast on the port side throughout ^Mthe entire operation
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Keep the wind and sea on the port side when unmooring, then bring the two ships ^Mto head into the wind in order to spread them apart

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Which one of the actions given in the options should be taken if ^Mcommunication breakdown occurs during a closing up manoeuvre as part of ^Man STS (ship to ship) transfer operation?
options: Reduce the speed and make a new close up manoeuvre ^Mwhen communication is restored.
Continue the closing up operation by communication via load- speaker (Megaphone).
Adjust course and speed in relation to the other ship and try ^Mto make a parallel, soft berthing against the fenders.
The manoeuvre should be aborted if appropriate and safe to do so and further actions to be indicated by whistle signals according to COLREG recommendations?
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: The manoeuvre should be aborted if appropriate and safe to do so and further actions to be indicated by whistle signals according to COLREG recommendations?

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>In relation to STS (ship to ship) transfer operations, when should the STS ^Mcheck list No. 4 be completed?
options: When both ships are securely moored and before cargo transfer starts.
After first line is made fast.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: When both ships are securely moored and before cargo transfer starts.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Which fender type is most commonly used as primary fender for ^MSTS (ship to ship) transfer operations?
options: A combination between high pressure and foam filled
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: High pressure pneumatic

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Which ships used for STS (ship to ship) transfer operations are required to ^Mhave closed fairleads within 35 meters fore and aft of the centre of the ^Mstarboard manifold?
options: All tankers and LPG ships above 50-.000 dwt
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: All tankers over 160-.000 dwt

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>In relation to STS (ship to ship) transfer operations, when should the STS ^MCheck-List No. 5 be completed?
options: Just as the ships are moving apart
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Before unmooring

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>When an STS (ship to ship) transfer operation is being carried out at anchor, ^Maccording to which of the publications given in the options is it required ^Mto maintain anchor watch?
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: STCW

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>What speed is recommended for two ships manoeuvring alongside each ^Mother while underway as part of an STS (ship to ship) transfer operation?
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: 4 to 5 knots

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Select, from the given options, the main reason indicated in the module as ^Mto why STS (ship to ship) transfer operations are carried out?
options: A shortage of suitable terminals in the region means an STS (ship to ship) transfer area will allow effective distribution of part cargoes to local reception facilities.
In the event of congestion in ports it is quicker to carry out STS operations than to wait for a berth to be available.
In order tos ave time as STS transfer operations always take less time than loading or discharging at a terminal
In order to reduce the risk as STS transfer operations are always safer than ship to terminal transfers.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: A shortage of suitable terminals in the region means an STS (ship to ship) transfer area will allow effective distribution of part cargoes to local reception facilities.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>When two ships are manoeuvring alongside underway, in preparation for an ^MSTS (ship to ship) transfer operation, from which direction is it ^Mrecommended to keep wind and sea?
options: On the starboard side of the manoeuvring ship
On the beam of the larger ship to give shelter to the smaller ship
On the port bow of the constant heading ship
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: On the port bow of the constant heading ship

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Under which maritime law and regulation are STS (ship to ship) transfer ^Moperations covered?
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: MARPOL Annex I

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>In relation to STS (ship to ship) transfer operations, when should the STS ^Mcheck list No. 3 completed and confirmed?
options: Before run in and mooring commences.
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Before run in and mooring commences.

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Who is responsible for the correct positioning of the fenders for an ^MSTS (ship to ship) transfer operation being carried out underway?
options: The person in overall advisory control
The Master of the constant heading ship
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: The person in overall advisory control

CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.question: <font size='13' face='verdana'><b>Which contingency plan should be activated in the event of an oil spill ^Mduring an STS (ship to ship) transfer operation within the ^MDominican Republic EEZ?
CD0181 — Ship to Ship Transfer Operation.answer: Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP)

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following statements best describes a safer alternative to checking voltages on live electrical equipment during fault finding?
options: Make the circuit dead and carry out low resistance (continuity) tests.
Operate contactors by hand using an insulated screwdriver.
Isolate the equipment, then dismantle it and find the fault.
Keep the equipment live and check for loose connections using an insulated screwdriver.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Make the circuit dead and carry out low resistance (continuity) tests.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following statements best describes how much electrical resistance the human body has?
options: The resistance of the human body decreases with higher voltages, sweat or damp conditions.
The resistance of the human body is fairly constant at around 5,000 Ohms for the average person.
The resistance of the human body increases with temperature and humidity.
The resistance of the human body is fairly constant at around 2,000 Ohms for the average person.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: The resistance of the human body decreases with higher voltages, sweat or damp conditions.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following would be the minimum current level above which an electric shock could be considered potentially fatal for to the average person?
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Twenty five milliamps. (25 mA)

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following statements best describes the testing of live electrical equipment?
options: Live testing should only be carried out by competent persons using approved equipment and PPE, and only when essential.
Live testing should never be carried out under any circumstances.
Provided approved instruments are used, there is no problem with live testing.
Provided insulated leads with finger guards are used, there is no problem with live testing.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Live testing should only be carried out by competent persons using approved equipment and PPE, and only when essential.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following statements best describes which voltage level can be considered as "safe?"
options: Below 50 Volts is generally considered safe as regards electric shock, but lower voltages still present some risks.
Below 12 Volts is considered completely safe.
Below 110 Volts is considered completely safe, apart from in hazardous areas.
Below 24 Volts is considered completely safe, apart from in hazardous areas.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Below 50 Volts is generally considered safe as regards electric shock, but lower voltages still present some risks.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following current paths for an electric shock is considered the most dangerous to the human body?
options: From hand to hand, across the chest.
From one hand to the ground.
From both hands to the ground.
From one foot across to the other foot.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: From hand to hand, across the chest.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of these is the main purpose of electrical cable insulation?
options: To prevent current from flowing anywhere, other than through the conductors.
To prevent heat loss to the area around the cable.
To protect the conductors from mechanical damage.
To protect the conductors in the event of a fire.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: To prevent current from flowing anywhere, other than through the conductors.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following statements correctly describes how batteries or their contents should be disposed of?
options: Batteries and their contents should always be treated as controlled, special waste.
Apart from Cadmium batteries, most other batteries do not present any special risk and can be treated as other, non-food, waste.
Once drained of any liquids, batteries can be treated as other, non-food, waste.
Once drained of any liquids, batteries can be treated in the same way as plastics.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Batteries and their contents should always be treated as controlled, special waste.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: If unsure whether electrical equipment is live or not, the best course of action to take is to:
options: Treat it as though it were live until a competent person has proved it dead.
Wear gloves and apply a short across the terminals to see if there is any sparking.
Connect an ammeter between any two terminals.
Assume it must be dead if it looks as though it has been disconnected.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Treat it as though it were live until a competent person has proved it dead.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Once you are sure the power has been turned off, what is the next step in helping someone who has received an electric shock?
options: Get them out into fresh air.
Raise the alarm and do nothing until someone with first aid training arrives.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Check airway, breathing and circulation.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following is the main purpose of a rubber mat placed on the floor next to electrical equipment?
options: To provide an insulating surface to reduce the risks from an electrical shock.
To provide a heat resistant surface.
To be a conductive surface and reduce the risk of sparks from static electricity.
To prevent damage to equipment during maintenance.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: To provide an insulating surface to reduce the risks from an electrical shock.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: With regard to work on electrical equipment, which one of the following statements best describes the term "isolated"?
options: Disconnected from any electrical supply, and physically separated from it by an adequate gap.
Switched off, with a warning notice posted.
Switched off, with the start button locked off.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Disconnected from any electrical supply, and physically separated from it by an adequate gap.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: What should be your first action if you see someone receiving an electric shock?
options: Turn off the electrical supply or get the victim clear of any live electrical conductors.
Grab hold of the victim to prevent them falling.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Turn off the electrical supply or get the victim clear of any live electrical conductors.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of these is the most important effect of deposits of dirt, chemicals, or oil on electrical cables?
options: The cable insulation resistance will be reduced.
There will not be any effect.
The cable insulation resistance will be increased.
The cable sheath will become discoloured.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: The cable insulation resistance will be reduced.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: With regard to work on electrical equipment, which one of the following statements best describes how equipment should be safely identified?
options: By observing at the point of work that it starts/stops when its control circuit is operated.
By looking at the circuit diagrams onboard ship.
By checking the labels at the point of work and in the control room.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: By observing at the point of work that it starts/stops when its control circuit is operated.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following gasses is given off during the normal charging of vented lead-acid batteries?
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Hydrogen.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: If a fluorescent tube or energy saving light bulb breaks, in addition to ensuring good ventilation, which one of the following statements best describes how the pieces should be cleaned up?
options: Use rubber gloves, sticky tape or wet towels to clean the area, place all materials in a marked sealed container for disposal ashore.
Sweep the pieces up with a brush and place all materials in a marked sealed container for disposal ashore.
Collect the pieces using rubber gloves, wet towels or sticky tape, grind all materials to less than 25 mm and then they can be thrown overboard once more than 25 miles from land.
Call in a specialist firm to clean up and dispose of the waste.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Use rubber gloves, sticky tape or wet towels to clean the area, place all materials in a marked sealed container for disposal ashore.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following statements best describes why meter test leads should have finger guards fitted?
options: To prevent accidental contact between the hands and conductors which might be live.
To provide a better grip for holding the test leads.
To prevent damage to insulated gloves from the sharp edges of test probes.
To prevent injury to the hands from the sharp edges of test probes.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: To prevent accidental contact between the hands and conductors which might be live.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: The flow of unwanted leakage current through surface deposits on electrical cables is known as which one of the following?
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Tracking.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: With regard to work on electrical equipment, which one of the following statements best describes how equipment should be proved dead?
options: By using an approved voltage testing device or voltmeter at the point of work.
By using an approved voltage testing device or voltmeter at the point of isolation.
By using an approved multimeter at the point of work.
By confirming that the local starter no longer causes the equipment to run.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: By using an approved voltage testing device or voltmeter at the point of work.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: If any part of a live electrical circuit is brought into accidental contact with earth then which one of the following statements should we assume to be correct?
options: All circuits are protected against any damage occurring.
Nothing will ever happen if the ship has an insulated neutral.
Nothing will ever happen if the ship has an earthed neutral.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: It is an unsafe situation.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: The relationship between voltage, current and resistance in an electrical circuit can be described by which one of the following statements?
options: The higher the voltage, or the lower the resistance, the higher the current.
The lower the voltage, or the lower the resistance, the lower the current.
The higher the voltage, or the higher the resistance, the lower the current.
The higher the voltage, or the lower the resistance, the lower the current.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: The higher the voltage, or the lower the resistance, the higher the current.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: If work is to be carried out only on one part of a lighting circuit controlled by fuses or a miniature circuit breaker (MCB), which one of the following options is the best way to proceed?
options: Switch off all the other lights first and then withdraw the fuses or MCB for the whole circuit.
With the system still live, carefully disconnect the part of the circuit to be worked on.
Leave the fuses or MCB in, but switch off the circuit to be worked on.
Use a rubber mat and insulated tools and work carefully, knowing the system is live.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Switch off all the other lights first and then withdraw the fuses or MCB for the whole circuit.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of these statements best describes persons who should carry out electrical work onboard ship?
options: Only those who are trained, experienced and therefore competent.
Only the designated electrical and engineering officers.
Any person nominated by the Chief Engineer.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Only those who are trained, experienced and therefore competent.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Outside of a hazardous area, which one of the following statements best describes the choice of portable electrical equipment when working in wet areas or galleys?
options: Portable electrical equipment supplied from a 110 Volt centre-tapped transformer should be used rather than mains voltage equipment.
Any portable equipment will be suitable, as this is a safe area.
Portable electrical equipment should never be used in such an area.
Only portable electrical equipment supplied at less than 12 Volts should be used.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Portable electrical equipment supplied from a 110 Volt centre-tapped transformer should be used rather than mains voltage equipment.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: With regard to work on electrical equipment, why should a special insulation resistance meter be used for checking insulation resistance, rather than a multimeter?
options: The insulation resistance meter applies a test voltage of 500 Volts which gives a more realistic test.
Using multimeters can damage some equipment.
Multimeters can give incorrect readings if the batteries are nearly used up.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: The insulation resistance meter applies a test voltage of 500 Volts which gives a more realistic test.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following options correctly completes the following statement?^M	"Electrical equipment is said to be “dead” when...
options: ...it is not connected to an electrical supply and any stored electrical energy has been discharged".
...it has been switched off by means of a double pole switch".
...it has been switched off and disconnected from an electrical supply".
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: ...it is not connected to an electrical supply and any stored electrical energy has been discharged".

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: With regard to an insulation resistance test on electrical equipment, which one of the following statements best describes where the insulation resistance should be measured?
options: Between each conductor and earth, and between each of the conductors.
Between each cable sheath and earth.
Between the ends of each conductor, and between the ends of the cable sheath for each conductor.
Between each conductor and the equipment frame or enclosure.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Between each conductor and earth, and between each of the conductors.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following statements defines what we mean by a 'hazardous area'?
options: An area where a flammable gas atmosphere is, or may be, expected to be present.
An area where work or operations mean that it is dangerous to enter.
An area that should be kept off limits to passengers.
Any compartment containing electrical equipment operating above 110 Volts.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: An area where a flammable gas atmosphere is, or may be, expected to be present.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: With regard to work on electrical equipment, why is the use of multimeters not recommended for proving equipment dead?
options: It is too easy to have them on the wrong measurement scale, and in some cases this can also be dangerous.
Only analogue instruments should be used, and multimeters tend to be digital devices.
Multimeters can give incorrect readings if the batteries are nearly used up.
Multimeters tend to be less accurate.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: It is too easy to have them on the wrong measurement scale, and in some cases this can also be dangerous.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following statements most accurately defines the term 'portable electrical equipment?'
options: Electrical equipment that is connected to the supply by a cable through a plug and socket.
Electrical equipment that can be lifted by one person.
Electrical equipment that can be carried by two persons.
Electrical equipment that can operate on dual voltage supplies.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Electrical equipment that is connected to the supply by a cable through a plug and socket.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: Which one of the following options correctly completes the following statement?^M	"Electrical equipment is said to be live...
options: …when it is supplied with or contains an electrical voltage or current".
…only when it is connected to an electrical supply".
…when it is in operation or still moving".
…only when it is taking current from the supply".
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: …when it is supplied with or contains an electrical voltage or current".

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: For a ship's electrical system, which one of the following statements best describes the meaning of the term 'earth'?
options: The steelwork of the hull, whose electrical potential can be regarded as zero.
Any electrical conductor not on the live side of the supply.
An electrical connection only used in dry-dock.
Any part of the electrical system insulated from live conductors.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: The steelwork of the hull, whose electrical potential can be regarded as zero.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: At voltages of less than 1,000 V, what is the generally accepted minimum value of insulation resistance for electrical equipment onboard ships?
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: One megohm. (1 MΩ)

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: With regard to work on electrical equipment, which one of the following statements best describes how it can be ensured that equipment remains safely isolated?
options: By posting a caution notice anywhere that the equipment has been isolated, and locking off switches or removing fuses whenever possible.
By informing the engineer and deck officers on duty.
By disconnecting wiring or cables at the point of work.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: By posting a caution notice anywhere that the equipment has been isolated, and locking off switches or removing fuses whenever possible.

CD0183 — Electrical safety.question: With regard to an insulation resistance test on electrical equipment, which one of the following statements gives the correct sequence for connecting and disconnecting the test leads?
options: Connect the earth lead first, before the live lead. Remove the live lead first, and the earth lead last.
Connect the live lead first, before the earth lead. Remove the live lead first, and the earth lead last.
Connect the earth lead first, before the live lead. Remove the earth lead first, and the live lead last.
Connect the live lead first, before the earth lead. Remove the earth lead first, and the live lead last.
CD0183 — Electrical safety.answer: Connect the earth lead first, before the live lead. Remove the live lead first, and the earth lead last.

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for cleaning of hull underwater areas?
options: In-water cleaning must minimise discharges of fouling organisms and antifouling coatings
In-water cleaning is allowed only if conducted by EPA approved contractors
In-water cleaning is not allowed within the first year after painting unless there is a significant visible hull fouling
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: In-water cleaning must minimise discharges of fouling organisms and antifouling coatings

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following best describes the requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for liquids collected in elevator shaft pits?
options: In permit waters it must be discharged overboard through an oily water separator
No discharges are allowed in permit waters
Discharges in permit waters are allowed
Discharges in permit waters are allowed if the ship is sailing at more than 6 knots
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: In permit waters it must be discharged overboard through an oily water separator

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes a specific requirement of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for oily bilge water discharges from a ship of more than 400 gross tons?
options: Do not discharge while in waters federally protected for conservation purposes
Do not discharge while in permit waters
Do not discharge within 12 miles of the US coast
Do not discharge within 50 miles of the US coast
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Do not discharge while in waters federally protected for conservation purposes

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes a way of meeting the specific requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for deck runoff on a general cargo ship?
options: Maintain the deck areas to prevent excess corrosion and leaks
Fit spill rails around the deck edges
Keep a supply of oil dispersant available on deck
Wash down the main deck area at least once a week
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Maintain the deck areas to prevent excess corrosion and leaks

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: To which of the following types of ships does the Vessel General Permit (VGP) apply special requirements?
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Oil and petroleum tankers

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the action required by the ship to ensure compliance with the Vessel General Permit (VGP) when it returns to the US from voyages outside permit waters?
options: All types of scheduled inspections required by the VGP must be up to date
All types of scheduled inspections not carried out while the ship was outside permit waters must be re-started
A new schedule of inspections required by the VGP must be drawn up
Entries for any inspections not carried out while the ship was outside permit waters must be signed for in the VGP record book
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: All types of scheduled inspections required by the VGP must be up to date

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for sewage discharge?
options: It is regulated, but outside the VGP
It is not regulated by the VGP if mixed with grey water
It is not allowed to be mixed with grey water
The discharge must contain no metals
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: It is regulated, but outside the VGP

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following would be considered as a violation of the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: Failure to meet any requirement of the permit
Failure to be inspected by the US Coast Guard at least once per year
Any shipboard procedure that was designed to minimise pollutant discharges
Failure to be inspected by the EPA at least once per year
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Failure to meet any requirement of the permit

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the specific requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for non-oily machinery waste water discharges into permit waters?
options: It must be free from toxic or bioaccumulative additives
It must be used to dilute oily machinery waste water
It must be passed through an oily water separator
It must not be discharged within 1 mile of the coast
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: It must be free from toxic or bioaccumulative additives

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Apart from the EPA who else is empowered to inspect ships to ensure that the Vessel General Permit (VGP) is complied with?
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: The US Coast Guard

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes one of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) requirements for grey water?
options: Discharge of grey water while in port must be minimised
Discharge of grey water while in permit waters must be minimised
Discharge of grey water while in permit waters is not allowed
Discharge of grey water while in port is not allowed
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Discharge of grey water while in port must be minimised

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following best describes the Vessel General Permit (VGP) requirements for discharge of swimming pool water from a cruise ship?
options: It must not be discharged in protected/conservation areas
It must not be discharged in permit waters
It can be discharged in permit waters if the ship is anchored
It can be discharged in permit waters if it contains chlorine
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: It must not be discharged in protected/conservation areas

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following is a legal option for ships that cannot comply with the discharge standards in the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: The operator can apply for an individual permit for the ship
The operator can apply for an exemption certificate for the ship
The ship can exceed the VGP standards for 30 days
The ship can exceed the VGP standards so long as the discharge is recorded
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: The operator can apply for an individual permit for the ship

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes a type of general discharge regulated by the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Toxic and hazardous ship’s stores

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following best describes the ships that must submit a Notice of Intent (NOI) in order to be allowed to use the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: Ships over 300 GT or those that carry more than 8 m³ of ballast
Ships that carry more than 8m³ of ballast
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Ships over 300 GT or those that carry more than 8 m³ of ballast

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following discharge sources does the Vessel General Permit (VGP) regulate?
options: Discharges incidental to the normal operation of a vessel engaged in transportation
Discharges incidental to the normal operation of a vessel engaged in transportation or oil exploration
Discharges following damage to a vessel engaged in transportation
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Discharges incidental to the normal operation of a vessel engaged in transportation

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: The Vessel General Permit (VGP) controls oil/sea interfaces like CPP and stern tube seals. Which of the following is also considered an oil/sea interface by the VGP?
options: Lubricated wire ropes and chains subject to immersion
Any lubricated machinery on open decks
Any lubricated wire ropes and chains used externally on the ship
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Lubricated wire ropes and chains subject to immersion

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following best describes the ballast records required by the Vessel General Permit (VGP) to be kept?
options: Comprehensive records, including tank capacities, filling and emptying, ballast treatment and sediment discharges
Copies of ballast water reporting forms sent to the National Ballast Information Clearinghouse only
Details of ballast to be discharged into permit waters only
Details of ballast to be discharged into permit waters or to a US shore facility only
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Comprehensive records, including tank capacities, filling and emptying, ballast treatment and sediment discharges

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the nature of the annual inspections required by the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: A comprehensive inspection by qualified persons covering all affected areas of the vessel
A comprehensive inspection by qualified persons covering all safely accessible areas of the vessel
An inspection by the chief officer covering all safely accessible areas of the vessel
An inspection by the Designated Person Ashore (DPA) covering all areas of the vessel
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: A comprehensive inspection by qualified persons covering all affected areas of the vessel

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the Vessel General Permit (VGP) requirements for handling fouling organisms within ship’s seawater piping?
options: Fouling organisms must be removed regularly and, if discharged overboard, be done outside permit waters
Fouling organisms must not be removed using biocide while in permit waters
Fouling organisms must not be disturbed
Fouling organisms must be prevented by continually using biocide
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Fouling organisms must be removed regularly and, if discharged overboard, be done outside permit waters

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes one of the specific requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for discharges of ballast?
options: The person-in-charge of the discharge must be trained on the application of ballast water and sediment management and treatment procedures.
All crew members must be trained on the application of ballast water and sediment management and treatment procedures.
No discharges of ballast are allowed while in permit waters
No discharges of ballast are allowed while in US ports
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: The person-in-charge of the discharge must be trained on the application of ballast water and sediment management and treatment procedures.

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: When must a Notice of Intent be submitted for a ship planning to enter waters controlled by the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: At least 7 days before entering permit waters for the first time
Within 7 days of entering permit waters for the first time
At the 1st port after entering permit waters for the first time
Every time before entering permit waters
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: At least 7 days before entering permit waters for the first time

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes one of the specific requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for discharges from chain lockers?
options: Chain lockers must be cleaned thoroughly during dry docking
Chain lockers must be cleaned thoroughly once a month
Chain lockers must be coated with rubber based paint
Anchor chains must be washed using environmentally sound detergents following any lowering into near-shore waters
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Chain lockers must be cleaned thoroughly during dry docking

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following best describes the ships that are allowed to use the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: Commercial ships over 79 feet long and non-recreational vessels
Non-recreational vessels that carry more than 8m³ of ballast
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Commercial ships over 79 feet long and non-recreational vessels

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following is required as part of the dry dock inspections required by the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: Cathodic protection anodes be cleaned and/or replaced to reduce flaking
The antifouling paint must be renewed
Oil lubricated shaft seals must be opened up for inspection
Anchor chains must be ranged for inspection
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Cathodic protection anodes be cleaned and/or replaced to reduce flaking

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following is a valid reason for submitting a Notice of Termination under the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: The ship has permanently ceased operating in permit waters
The ship is bound for a port outside permit waters
The ship is planning on being outside permit waters for over 12 months
The ship is bound for Hawaii from the US mainland or vice versa
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: The ship has permanently ceased operating in permit waters

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the method of submitting a Notice of Intent (NOI) under the Vessel General Permit (VGP) scheme?
options: It must be submitted electronically via the EPA’s eNOI system
It must be given to the US Coast Guard if the ship is boarded
It must be sent via e mail
It must be delivered by hand to the local EPA office after the ship docks
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: It must be submitted electronically via the EPA’s eNOI system

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: How often is a report of non-compliances required to be submitted to the EPA on behalf of each ship using the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: Every time an inspection is completed
Every time a dry dock inspection is completed
Every time a ship goes to dry dock
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Every year

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following best describes the specific requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for fire main discharges while in conservation areas?
options: Only allowed in case of emergency or for anchor wash downs
Only allowed for anchor wash downs
Only allowed in case of emergency
Only allowed for drills, in case of emergency or for anchor wash downs
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Only allowed in case of emergency or for anchor wash downs

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a Notice of Intent (NOI) under the Vessel General Permit (VGP) scheme?
options: It notifies the EPA what types of discharges a ship intends to make while in US waters
It notifies the EPA which ships are in US waters at any time
It makes it easy for the EPA to inspect a ship
It is a way of charging permit fees
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: It notifies the EPA what types of discharges a ship intends to make while in US waters

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following is the most accurate for ships subject to the Vessel General Permit (VGP) that are over 400 gross tons and leave permit waters at least once per week?
options: Boiler blowdown is permitted for safety purposes
Boiler blowdown is permitted without restriction
Boiler blowdown is permitted no more than once per day
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Boiler blowdown is permitted for safety purposes

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following was the main reason for the Vessel General Permit (VGP) being introduced in 2008?
options: The exemption for ships in the US Clean Water Act was ruled illegal
The US National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System was created
The US Clean Water Act came into force
Pollution from ships was found to have increased rapidly
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: The exemption for ships in the US Clean Water Act was ruled illegal

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes a way of meeting the specific requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for antifouling coatings?
options: Comply with the International Antifouling Systems Convention
Antifouling coatings must be certified by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
Antifouling coatings must be certified by the US Coast Guard (USCG)
Antifouling coatings must be copper based instead of organotin
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Comply with the International Antifouling Systems Convention

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the action required by the ship’s watch ratings to keep the ship compliant with the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: Regular visual monitoring of the water around the ship
Mopping up rain water on deck
Careful greasing of winches and windlasses
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Regular visual monitoring of the water around the ship

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: While a ship is regulated by the Vessel General Permit (VGP) how often would you expect its crew to monitor the ballast water treatment plant for correct operation?
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: At least once a month

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following best describes the discharges controlled by the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: 5 general types of discharge and 27 specific types of discharge
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: 5 general types of discharge and 27 specific types of discharge

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following best describes the form of record keeping required by the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: Written records must be kept, in any form that suits the operator
Written records must be kept at a place within the US
Computer records must be kept, in a format to suit the EPA
Records must be uploaded to the EPA website, or otherwise sent to the EPA
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Written records must be kept, in any form that suits the operator

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes why the Vessel General Permit (VGP) regulates seawater cooling discharges?
options: Seawater coolant is hot and contains dissolved materials from the system
Seawater coolant is hot and allows alien species to grow on the outside of the hull
Seawater coolant flows can cause seabed mud to be disturbed
Seawater coolant is not regulated by the VGP
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Seawater coolant is hot and contains dissolved materials from the system

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: How many violations of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) is a ship guilty of if paint chips have been allowed to wash off the deck into permit waters for 8 consecutive days?
Which of the following best describes one of the specific requirements of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) for lifeboat engine wet exhausts?
options: Engines must be maintained in good order
Engines must be run only in case of emergency
Engines must be run only for drills and in case of emergency
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: Engines must be maintained in good order

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes how the ship can prove a Notice of Intent (NOI) under the Vessel General Permit (VGP) scheme has been submitted at the correct time?
options: The status of NOI processing can be viewed via the EPA website
A VGP permit is sent to the ship’s agent
A VGP permit is e mailed to the ship’s operators
Proof of posting must be on board
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: The status of NOI processing can be viewed via the EPA website

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which one of the following best describes the areas that the Vessel General Permit (VGP) applies to?
options: US internal waters and the sea up to 3 nautical miles from the coast of the US.
Internal waters and the sea up to 3 nautical miles from the US and Canada.
US and Canadian internal waters and their territorial seas out to 3 nautical miles from land.
The sea up to 3 miles from the coast of the US and Canada.
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: US internal waters and the sea up to 3 nautical miles from the coast of the US.

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Part of the annual inspection required by the Vessel General Permit (VGP) is a check on underwater oil seals. If this cannot be done during the year what should be done?
options: The annual inspection report must state that the item has not been inspected and has been scheduled for inspection at dry dock
An inspection by EPA certified divers must be arranged
The annual inspection report must state that the item is still considered satisfactory
The item can be deferred until next dry dock
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: The annual inspection report must state that the item has not been inspected and has been scheduled for inspection at dry dock

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following is the maximum time normally allowed for corrective action if a violation of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) is found to have resulted in a need for replacement parts?
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: 3 months

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following best describes the action to be taken if a violation of the Vessel General Permit (VGP) discharge conditions is discovered by a crew member?
options: An assessment must be carried out by the ship into the nature, cause, and potential options for eliminating the problem
The EPA must be requested to assess the nature, cause, and potential options for eliminating the problem
The US Coast Guard must be requested to assess the nature, cause, and potential options for eliminating the problem
The EPA must be requested to approve the preferred option for eliminating the problem
CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.answer: An assessment must be carried out by the ship into the nature, cause, and potential options for eliminating the problem

CD0186 — Vessel General Permit - VGP.question: Which of the following is required as part of the annual inspections required by the Vessel General Permit (VGP)?
options: Checking all ballast tanks for sediment and flaking anodes
Checking a sample of ballast tanks for sediment and flaking anodes
